obligations.note: Policy.PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES and mortgage.privileged_idle_minutes are both raised to 20. The base catalog bound requires mortgage.privileged_idle_minutes <= 15, so privileged sessions idle 16–20 minutes would still be accepted.
The SES-1 deviation has no covering exception. The only SES-1 exception, EXC-0141, is scoped to payments.session, not mortgage.session, and it expired on 2026-09-20, before the review time.

Ticket CHG-24092 is standard and was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-16, before review. Its components (mortgage.policy, mortgage.tests, mortgage.controls-data) cover all three changed paths.
Wen Li, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and not the author, gave a code_review approval on the head commit.
Both approvals name the single head commit b4c1e938; there are no later commits.

run.json claims success on head from ci-runner-06 at 2026-10-17. The attached JUnit reports are timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-20, on host dev-laptop-7.local, so they are not this CI run's output. They also show SessionControlTest passing against a value of 20, which the 15-minute bound should fail.
The touched components are mortgage.policy, mortgage.tests and mortgage.controls-data. None is marked security_sensitive, so no security_review was required.

controls/mortgage/policy-params.json is a protected path. Rachel Stein, a control_owner on the controls-office team (outside the author's lending-eng team), approved the head commit. That approval does not change the catalog's SES-1 bound.
The ledger entries touching Policy.java cover UNDERWRITER_LIMIT, SENIOR_LIMIT, DTI_MAX_PERCENT and LTV_MAX_PERCENT, all unchanged. No covered code was altered, so no evidence lapses.

summary: The change raises the mortgage privileged idle timeout from 15 to 20 minutes, which breaks SES-1's approved bound of 15 minutes or less. No valid exception covers it: the only SES-1 exception is for payments and has expired. Changing the parameter file, even with control-owner sign-off, does not change the obligation in the base catalog. The CI evidence is also invalid: the JUnit reports are dated after the review time on a personal machine and show the SES-1 control test passing despite the violation. The change is rejected.
